statement: Let key(t) = (|t - x|, t), compared lexicographically. Let cnt_r(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = v, and let cnt_arr(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(arr) and arr[i] = v. The function returns a result r such that: (1) len(r) = k; (2) r is nondecreasing, i.e. r[i] <= r[j] for all 0 <= i < j < len(r); (3) cnt_r(v) <= cnt_arr(v) for every integer v; and (4) for all integers a,b, if cnt_r(a) > 0 and cnt_r(b) < cnt_arr(b), then key(a) <= key(b).
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order (for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(arr), arr[i] <= arr[j]); len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000 for every 0 <= i < len(arr); and -10000 <= x <= 10000.

statement: Under the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or get stuck.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order (for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(arr), arr[i] <= arr[j]); len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000 for every 0 <= i < len(arr); and -10000 <= x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = k.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] <= r[j].
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the number of occurrences of v in r is at most the number of occurrences of v in arr.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer a that occurs at least once in r and every integer b that occurs fewer times in r than in arr, we have |a - x| < |b - x|, or |a - x| = |b - x| and a <= b.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an integer s with 0 <= s <= len(arr) - k such that r is exactly the length-k sequence arr[s], arr[s+1], ..., arr[s+k-1]; in particular len(r) = k and r[i] = arr[s+i] for all 0 <= i < k.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v that occurs at least once in r, every integer u with |u - x| < |v - x| occurs equally many times in r and in arr.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), arr[0] <= r[i] <= arr[len(arr)-1].
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if x <= arr[0], then len(r) = k and r[i] = arr[i] for every i with 0 <= i < k.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if x >= arr[len(arr)-1], then len(r) = k and r[i] = arr[len(arr)-k+i] for every i with 0 <= i < k.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.

statement: Consider two calls with the same arr and k, using x = x1 and x = x2. If the first call returns r1 and the second returns r2, then len(r1) = len(r2) = k and for every i with 0 <= i < k, r1[i] <= r2[i].
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values satisfy -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; and x1 <= x2 both satisfy -10000 <= x1,x2 <= 10000.

statement: If the call on (arr,k,x) returns r and the call on (arr2,k,x2) returns r2, then len(r2) = len(r) = k and r2[i] = r[i] + t for every i with 0 <= i < k.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000. Let t be an integer, arr2 a slice of the same length with arr2[i] = arr[i] + t for all i, and x2 = x + t; suppose both (arr,k,x) and (arr2,k,x2) satisfy the preconditions and no i64 overflow occurs in these additions.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist k distinct indices p_0, p_1, ..., p_{k-1} with 0 <= p_j < len(arr) such that r is the nondecreasing rearrangement of the sequence arr[p_0], arr[p_1], ..., arr[p_{k-1}]; equivalently, len(r) = k and the multiset of values of r equals the multiset of values at those k array positions.
preconditions: arr is sorted in nondecreasing order; len(arr) >= 1; 1 <= k <= len(arr); len(arr) <= 10000; values and x satisfy -10000 <= arr[i], x <= 10000.
